title: Collections, Iteration, and LINQ
summary: Use arrays, List, Dictionary, HashSet, foreach, generic types, and LINQ without hiding mutation or repeated enumeration.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Collections, Iteration, and LINQ
Use compiler and runtime evidence to test the contract
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Arrays have fixed length; `List<T>` provides an ordered resizable sequence; `Dictionary<TKey,TValue>` maps unique keys; `HashSet<T>` enforces uniqueness. Generics preserve element types. `foreach` expresses value traversal, while an indexed loop is appropriate when position matters. LINQ operators such as `Where`, `Select`, and `Average` describe queries and often use deferred execution, meaning results may reflect later source changes. Materialize with `ToList` when a stable snapshot is required. Do not structurally modify a collection during its enumeration.
keyPoints: Arrays have fixed length; `List<T>` provides an ordered resizable sequence; `Dictionary<TKey,TValue>` maps unique keys; `HashSet<T>` enforces uniqueness.
commonMistakes: index equal to Length is invalid
changing a list during foreach invalidates enumeration
